name: Stone Verse
memo: Audioslave - Like a Stone: verse/intro. Clean, single-coil style tone with chorus and a long delay, in the spirit of Tom Morello's clean sound.

band.style_feel: slow, spacious mid-tempo groove, kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, open ride/hi-hat in the verses
band.key: unconfirmed (sources disagree: G minor / C major); play by ear with the recording
parts: Part A: intro and verse - clean guitar, sparse drums
Part B: pre-chorus - drums and bass build
Part C: chorus - full band, big and open
Part D: solo - heavy drums, driving
Part E: final chorus and outro - full band
band.tips: Tempo estimates range about 108-112 BPM (Musicnotes lists 112, other analyses 108-109). Play the intro cleanly for 2 bars before the Trio+ starts learning, and keep strumming steady.

whammy.tuning: Drop D (D A D G B E) is commonly cited for Audioslave, but this song's tuning is not confirmed (one chord site lists standard)
how: Turn the left knob to 2 OCT UP.
Leave the WHAMMY footswitch off until the solo.
Switch it on at the solo and rock the heel-toe pedal for the squeals.
If you want Drop D, retune only your 6th string down to D; the Whammy DT cannot make true Drop D.
whammy.tips: The Whammy is part of the Like a Stone solo sound per several gear guides; the exact interval is not documented, so set it by ear (OCT UP is a tamer alternative).

originals.guitar: Fender Stratocaster-style 'Soul Power' guitar with Ibanez Edge tremolo

guitar.position: neck pickup for the clean verse; bridge pickup for chorus and solo, volume full
guitar.tone_notes: Gear guides recommend single-coil pickups, with the neck pickup for a smoother tone. With humbuckers, roll back the gain a little and use the neck pickup.

name: Stone Chorus
memo: Audioslave - Like a Stone: chorus. Crunchy, open and full, with a flat-EQ style boost.

name: Stone Solo
memo: Audioslave - Like a Stone: solo. High-gain lead with a Helldrive-style overdrive after the Whammy, plus delay.
